data.gender_notes: Lavkesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lavkesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Lav' (God's grace) and 'Kesh' (hair or divine gift). It is believed that a child named Lavkesh is blessed with God's grace and divine protection. The name Lavkesh carries the meaning “God's grace, divine gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lavkesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace, divine gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Lav Keshav Mitra was a prominent Bengali scholar and social reformer who lived in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was a strong advocate for widow remarriage and women's education. Mitra founded the Brahmo Samaj, a religious and social reform movement influenced by the ideas of Rammohun Roy, which sought to purify Hinduism and promote social progress.
historical_references.context: Religious and social reform movement in Bengal

historical_references.reference: Another Lav Kesh, a king of the Sisodia Rajput clan in Rajasthan, ruled during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. He is known for his military campaigns against invading Mughal forces and his patronage of art and literature. One of his most notable achievements was the construction of the Rani Sikri fort and the adjacent temple complex, which remains a popular tourist destination in Rajasthan today.
historical_references.context: Mughal invasions and artistic patronage in Rajasthan
